topics.title: Exam Core: The Paper in One Page

modes.blurb: The real paper, part by part: a label, 10 true/false, a French match, an Italian match.
modes.why: Same order and shape as the midterm. Part 1 puts one label in front of you with five questions; Part 2 is ten true/false, half on aromas and half on the introduction; Parts 3 and 4 are one five-pair match each. Every run prefers what you have not mastered yet, so repeat it until the bank runs dry.
modes.title: Mock exam
Exam core
modes.blurb: The highest-yield facts from all four parts.
modes.why: One pass over what decides each part: the label terms, the aroma stages, the French grapes and the Italian designations.

modes.title: True or false
modes.blurb: Part 2 is all true/false. Drill the swapped facts.
modes.why: A false statement here is a true one with one fact swapped for its neighbour: malic for tartaric, primary for tertiary, Côte de Nuits for Côte de Beaune.

modes.title: Matching
modes.blurb: Region to grape, designation to region — like Parts 3 and 4.
modes.why: Every pool has spare answers and some answers repeat, so you cannot get the last pair by elimination. Know each pair cold.

modes.title: Read the label
modes.blurb: A label in front of you: what is each part?
modes.why: Part 1. Designation vs producer vs vineyard vs commercial name, and Riserva vs Superiore vs Classico.

modes.title: Label cards
modes.blurb: One real-style label, five questions about it.
modes.why: Part 1 of the paper: read the label in front of you, then answer without guessing from the wording.
